summary: Does the tree have a root-to-leaf path whose node values sum to targetSum?
mainInsight: Subtract each node's value from the remaining target on the way down; at a LEAF check whether the remainder is exactly 0.
canonicalApproach: Recursive DFS with a remaining sum

approaches.name: Recursive DFS with a remaining sum
approaches.summary: Pass target - val to the children; test at leaves.

personalSolution.approach: Recursive DFS with a remaining sum

promptVariants: How do you track the required sum while descending?
Which pattern fits root-to-leaf path sums?
options: Pass down the remaining target (target - node.val)
Sum all the values first, then compare with target
Use a heap of the partial sums along each path
Sort the path values and compare with the target
cards.answer: Pass down the remaining target (target - node.val)
cards.explanation: A leaf succeeds iff the remaining value is exactly 0 after subtracting its value.

incorrectOptionExplanations.Sort the path values and compare with th: Order is fixed by the tree.

promptVariants: Why must the test happen at a leaf, not at any node?
What goes wrong if you test at every node?
cards.answer: The problem asks for root-to-LEAF paths. A partial path that sums to the target but continues to a leaf does not count. Testing at every node would accept paths ending at internal nodes (wrong).
keyPoints: Path must end at a leaf
cards.explanation: Negative values mean you cannot prune when the remaining sum becomes negative.
Each node is visited at most once.

promptVariants: Complete the statement: Recursion stack space: ___
Why is the empty tree special?
options: False (there is no root-to-leaf path at all)
True, because the sum 0 is matched by an empty path
An error, since the root node is missing here
None, since there is no path to evaluate at all
cards.answer: False (there is no root-to-leaf path at all)
cards.explanation: An empty tree has no paths at all, even when the target is 0.
